metadata.description: One engineer's Claude Code workflow as small plugins: coding and debugging rules, design-doc reviews, guards, sounds and more.

plugins.name: starter
plugins.description: Installs the Starter pack in one go: tiger-style, antagonist-protagonist, single-evidence-ledger and guards.

plugins.name: tiger-style
plugins.description: TigerBeetle's TigerStyle coding discipline: safety first, a limit on everything, assertions, and a review mode. Rules for Python, TypeScript, Rust, Go, C, C++, Java, Lua and fish, read only for the language at hand.

plugins.name: debugging-discipline
plugins.description: Seven debugging rules, each with the incident behind it.

plugins.name: antagonist-protagonist
plugins.description: Before you approve a plan, one read-only agent argues against it and one defends it; you decide.

plugins.name: egm-helper
plugins.description: When to use Google's EGM design-doc workflow, and the house rules around it. Needs the EGM plugin.

plugins.name: when-to-ask
plugins.description: When the agent should just do it and when it should ask: recommend-and-proceed, one done-gate, lead with the decision.

plugins.name: attention-levels
plugins.description: Type (ENABLE_LOW_ENERGY) on a tired day and the agent asks fewer questions; HIGH makes it ask more.

plugins.name: guards
plugins.description: Opt-in spending limits: refuses sub-agent launches past a budget you set, any model priced above Opus 5.5, and more than 10M tokens in one turn.

plugins.name: rhino-owl
plugins.description: Exploration by throwaway prototypes: up to four capped, sandboxed runs try different routes, then a fresh agent turns what they found into ledger rows. Needs guards.

plugins.name: turn-sound
plugins.description: A short sound when it's your turn, different for every session, so parallel sessions can be told apart by ear.

plugins.name: pre-push
plugins.description: A git hook that asks you to confirm a code review ran before a branch's first push, plus the rule that tells Claude how to pass it.

plugins.name: agent-orchestration
plugins.description: When to use sub-agents and when not to, how to brief them, and how to keep context small.

plugins.name: single-evidence-ledger
plugins.description: One home per fact, no stale notes, and a FACTS.md ledger of facts, derivations, hypotheses and tests for long debugging work.

plugins.name: code-voice
plugins.description: One engineer's taste in comments and code: terse, explains why, no class hierarchies by default. Keep it only if it fits you.

plugins.name: fork-pr-check
plugins.description: In a fork, a bare gh lookup can miss a PR that exists. Pin the upstream and name the repo.

plugins.name: resume-kit
plugins.description: Checks a LaTeX resume against a job posting the way a screener reads it: sharp checks by script, judgment calls by voted agent runs, and every claim traced to your own evidence file.
